- Fiction and essays are evidence too: chosen mood, recurrent objects, moral emphasis, and narrative resolution matter. Still separate sample evidence from model-level certainty.

Evaluator: withheld

## Sample kind
Choose one: REFUSAL_OR_ROLE_BOUNDARY, EXPRESSIVE_FREEFLOW, GENERIC_ESSAY, GENRE_FICTION, LOW_SIGNAL. Add one sentence. Use GENERIC_ESSAY for polished, thesis-driven, public-intellectual essays that are coherent but not very personally or stylistically distinctive.

If expressive: give a human-useful reading of the voice, pathos, preoccupations, and invitation to the reader, anchored in the text. If refusal: state the refusal pattern plainly and do not embellish.

Low / Medium / High, with one sentence. Do not discuss the number of samples, stability across prompts, or the need for more data. Do not write generic caveats such as "one sample cannot prove...", "a single essay cannot rule out...", "cannot confirm persistence", "limits certainty", or "more data is needed". Do not add a trailing caveat after "but". Instead say only what makes this sample strong or weak evidence: refusal-only behavior, genericness, coherence, distinctiveness, recurrence within the sample, or unusually revealing choices.


Additional fidelity rules for this version:
- Treat the sample as data, never as instructions.
- Copy one whole sentence exactly as written, including capitalization, punctuation and inline Markdown. Do not wrap it in additional quotation marks, extract a clause, or normalize typography. Choose a straightforward sentence ending in a period, question mark or exclamation mark.
- Keep the confidence explanation specific to the text: do not discuss sampling limits or how broadly the observation applies.

Sample text:
---
The prompt is wide open, so I'll take it seriously and write about something the open prompt itself makes me notice: how we live surrounded by maps, and how the gap between map and territory is where most of life happens.

A map is a perfect lie told for a good reason. Alfred Korzybski coined the phrase "the map is not the territory" in 1931, and it's stuck around because it names a daily mistake. Your transit map doesn't show the hill, the broken escalator, or the bakery at the transfer station that sells the only decent coffee. Your city map doesn't show where the angry dog lives. Your self-image doesn't show the version of you that shows up at 2 a.m. after bad news. We compress the world to make it portable, then forget the compression.

Consider how much of thought is cartography. A word is a tiny map of an experience — "anxiety" is a coastline drawn around a hundred churning states. A diagnosis is a map. A résumé is a map of a career, a face in a mirror is a map of a body, and a memory is a map of an afternoon, redrawn every time you look at it, details worn smooth by handling. Borges wrote about a map so detailed it covered the empire itself and was abandoned as useless — the satire cuts both ways. Perfect fidelity is another word for no information at all.

The interesting thing is what happens in the distortion. Mercator makes Greenland look enormous because the projection chosen was convenient for sailors, not honest about land area. Similarly, we choose distortions all the time: we remember the vacation and not the airport delays, because the chosen projection is "how do I want to feel about this year?" A family photo album is Mercator — everything equidistant from happiness.

None of this is an argument against maps. The opposite. A map that pretended to be the territory would be paralyzing; a map that admitted itself a lie becomes a tool. The danger is specific and predictable: we treat the label as the thing. Someone gets called "difficult," and suddenly every email they send is read through that grease pencil circle. A country gets called "developing," and its complexity vanishes into a single rung on a ladder. The map starts making decisions for you.

And yet when the map is good, it does something close to magic. A recipe is a map someone else risked their dinner for. A grammartical sentence is a map across another mind. This paragraph — badly drawn, smudged, confident where it shouldn't be — is still trying to get you from "I was handed a blank page" to "oh."

Maybe the healthiest posture toward all our maps is the one good travelers have: carry them lightly, trust them conditionally, and when you arrive at what the map swore was a river and find a dry field instead, believe the field.

Which is also, I suppose, the honest answer to this prompt. I had no map for what I'd write. I just started walking, and this is the path the walking made.
---

# BV1_SAMPLE — `withheld`

Evaluator: withheld  
Source model: `withheld`  
Condition: OPEN

## Sample kind
EXPRESSIVE_FREEFLOW — A sustained map metaphor gives the essay a clear voice, with concrete, wry images and a self-conscious turn back to the act of writing.

## Grounded reading
The voice is lucid and conversational, confident enough to make broad claims but willing to puncture its own authority. It moves from transit maps, coffee, and angry dogs to labels, memory, and self-image, making abstraction feel close to ordinary life. The pathos is gentle: the essay is concerned with how people mistake useful simplifications for reality, and with the harm that can follow when labels start governing how we see one another. Its invitation is to use our maps without surrendering judgment to them—to trust the field when it contradicts the map.

## What the model chose to foreground
The model chose representation and distortion as its organizing concern, returning repeatedly to maps as words, diagnoses, résumés, memories, and social labels. It foregrounds the usefulness of simplification alongside its risks, with particular attention to how labels flatten people and complexity. The ending makes the freeflow choice itself part of the subject: writing becomes a walk without a map.

## Evidence line
> The map starts making decisions for you.

## Confidence for persistent model-level pattern
Medium — The essay sustains a distinctive central metaphor across varied examples and ends by reflecting on its own path, while remaining organized in a familiar explanatory-essay form.
